messages.subject: Goodness-of-Fit of an Occupancy Model
parts:
Greetings fellows hierarchical ecologists,

I am fitting a model of weekly site occupancy by mosquitoes with a data set of four years. I am really interested on getting a measure of goodness-of-fit from the model, but don't know how to select the proper discrepancy measure to calculate the Bayesian p-value.

My secondary occasions(i.e. visits, etc) are different traps on an area where mosquito presence is expected to be homogeneous. The data is aggregated over rows of the detection history array. So, I have information on the number of traps and positives traps per site and per week, e.g.:

# Positive Traps       Week    Site      # Traps
 0                               1          1         1
 0                               1          2         3
 1                               1          3         3
 2                               2          1         4
 0                               2          2         4
 3                               2          3         5

I have tried to use both Chi-square and squared deviation as the discrepancy measures, but both resulted in Bayesian p-value that I found difficult to believe. My guess is that the problem is in the value that I'm using as the expected one to calculate the discrepancy. Currently, I am using "Psi[site,week] * #Traps[site,week] * p[week]" as the expected value.

I am aware that Kery & Royle's Big Book states that aggregate data over detection history is the best way for getting goodness-of-fit measures, but I am not sure if it would apply even if the data is already aggregated over rows (then I would have to aggregate over combinations of # Positive Traps and # Traps). Even if it would be the case, I would not be sure of the best expected value.

Thank you all for dedicating time of your days for helping,  

--
Guilherme Barradas Mores
Biólogo, Mestrando do Programa de Pós-Graduação em Ecologia da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul
